The zero residual establishes Y-coordinate alignment for these four positions. It is a coordinate difference, not a gradient. This section distinguishes three response laws: a sharp threshold with exact inactivity below it, the original tanh approximation with a signed response below threshold, and an optional smooth law with exact inactivity. Smoothness of a scalar switch and smoothness of its composition with a gradient magnitude are separate questions. None establishes a solution to the Clay Mathematics Institute Navier–Stokes problem.
Velocity field, time, and spatial gradient in a specified continuous domain.
Modeled field; its regularity and coupling need specifying.
Euclidean gradient magnitude; not differentiable as a function of the gradient at zero.
Threshold in gradient units; τ₀/η is an optional dimensionally compatible calibration.
Gradient regularization scale in gδ; same units as the gradient. Distinct from a Dirac delta.
Sharp exact-off, original signed tanh, and optional smooth exact-off response laws.

Choose the response law a before using the equation. Sharp threshold: a₀(q) = max(q, 0), so the added force is zero for q ≤ 0 and proportional to q for q > 0. This law is continuous but not differentiable at q = 0.

Original tanh choice: aₜ(q) = q[1 + tanh(q/ε)]/2, with ε > 0. It is smooth as a function of q, but for finite q < 0 it is negative and nonzero. For example, aₜ(−ε) ≈ −0.119203ε. The force therefore reverses direction below threshold when σ > 0; it does not simply switch off. A small tail may be intentional, but its sign and interpretation must be stated.

Zero-gradient concern: |v| is not differentiable at v = 0. Composing it with tanh does not automatically remove that issue; a particular composition can have cancellations, which need checking. For a smooth alternative, use gδ(v) = √(v · v + δ²) − δ with δ > 0, and qδ = gδ(∇S) − Γcrit. This changes the gradient measure near zero and is a modeling choice.

Optional smooth exact-off response: aε(q) = 0 for q ≤ 0, and aε(q) = q exp[−(ε/q)²] for q > 0. For fixed ε > 0 this scalar function is C∞, including the join at zero. Using aε(qδ) with fixed δ > 0 makes the constitutive response smooth in the gradient variable and exactly zero when qδ ≤ 0. This is an alternative to the tanh law, not a property of it. Its positive onset in the original magnitude is |∇S| > √(Γcrit² + 2δΓcrit), so the threshold must be calibrated in the chosen measure. To retain the original cutoff |∇S| = Γcrit instead, use the calibrated excess qδ* = √(|∇S|² + δ²) − √(Γcrit² + δ²). It has the same sign as |∇S| − Γcrit for Γcrit ≥ 0. Using aε(qδ*) gives a smooth exact-off alternative with that original cutoff; the response above it is still a changed constitutive law.

A fixed eₖ specifies direction; it does not guarantee drag or energy dissipation. For f to remove kinetic energy pointwise, u · f must be nonpositive. The model still needs a domain, initial and boundary data, a definition or equation for S, and compatible coefficient units. A smooth constitutive response is not a proof of smooth solutions for all time. Pressure, viscosity, yield, and boundary remain modeling language unless independently operationalized.

Name the result and its domain: smoothness of the response function in its argument, or a property of the initial field at initialization. Neither description, by itself, establishes a theorem about subsequent evolution. A response function can be smooth for every scalar argument while global PDE regularity remains unestablished here. An initial-field identity reported without its derivation should retain that attribution; reporting it is not independent verification.

Treats status or context as a signed field over a specified spatial embedding. Advection carries the field, diffusion spreads it, and a localized source changes it. A network alone does not specify the continuous geometry needed for these derivatives. With constant D_diff ≥ 0 and ∇ · u = 0, the following transport form is also a conservative continuity form.
A(t) = ∫₀ᵗ γ[U(s) − Ubaseline] ds,     J(t) = κ A(t).

Kₕ is a smooth localized kernel of width h > 0 with spatial integral 1. The original δ(x − x₀) is an alternative point-source idealization interpreted as a distribution, not an ordinary smooth function. A stores accumulated input; κ converts that stored quantity to a source rate with the required units. This retains the original memory choice explicitly. Under closed or periodic boundaries, constant positive excess utility can make the total field grow quadratically in time because the stored input is integrated again by the evolution equation. If instantaneous production is intended instead, specify J(t) = γ[U(t) − Ubaseline] with suitable units; that is a different model. Negative excess input may lower this signed field. Initial and boundary data remain necessary. For compressible transport, replace u · ∇S by ∇ · (Su).
Constant diffusion coefficient, with units length²/time.
Smooth localized source kernel, width h > 0, integral 1; units inverse spatial volume.
Optional Dirac point-source distribution replacing Kₕ; not a smooth ordinary function.

The sharp version defines exactly what happens on both sides: the additional boundary force is zero at and below threshold, and active above it. Zero added force does not mean the whole system is stable; the other terms still evolve. The smooth alternatives and their distinct behavior are specified in the earlier threshold section.

T is the symmetric viscous stress for the stated incompressible Newtonian analogy. The earlier µ₀∇u was a scaled velocity-gradient tensor, not this full stress. This constitutive choice does not establish literal fluid behavior in a social system.
Γcrit ≥ 0. Optional calibration: Γcrit = τ₀/η, with τ₀ ≥ 0 and η > 0.
q = |∇S| − Γcrit;     a₀(q) = 0 if q ≤ 0, and a₀(q) = q if q > 0.

Assume constant ρ > 0, µ > 0, and σ ≥ 0; p = P/ρ and ν = µ/ρ connect this equation to the earlier normalized form. The calibration η must give Γcrit the same units as |∇S|. Increasing η lowers Γcrit at fixed τ₀, so the label rigidity does not by itself establish stronger resistance. Fixed-direction forcing is not necessarily dissipative. Initial and boundary data, the S coupling, and a domain are required; smooth activation alone does not establish well-posedness or global regularity.
Calibration scale with units chosen so τ₀/η is a gradient. Rigidity is an interpretive label.
Pressure variable; −∇P is a pressure-gradient force, not an equilibrium guarantee.

\quad\lambda_p=\frac{\eta B_p}{P_*+\eta B_p+P_{raw,p}}.
Q_{write}(x)=\frac{\eta Q_v(x)}{1+\alpha(x)}R_h^*\{V_p\chi_p^w\}.
It satisfies 0≤Q_write≤ηQ_v pointwise and ∫Q_write dx=ΣV_pΣY ṁ. No energy is counted twice. The release when expression fades is
\partial_t\theta+\nabla\cdot(u\theta+j_T)
=Q_v-Q_{write}+R_h^*\{V_pP_{release,p}\}.

Temperature represents an explicit mechanical/thermal transfer channel; it is not assigned a hydration or electrical meaning. These constitutive coefficients are temperature-independent, so thermal expansion is absent rather than silently included. Mechanical work changes the thermal field and structure changes conduction; temperature is not claimed to feed back on elasticity in this chosen branch.
## 8. Numerical method and what the tests must distinguish

Velocity and temperature use Fourier collocation, a strict two-thirds retained-mode cutoff, periodic Gaussian-smoothed material interpolation and its adjoint stress spreading. The velocity equation uses the rotational form u×curl u and a Leray projection; the reported physical pressure subtracts the kinetic-energy pressure offset. Material velocity gradients are the derivatives of the same interpolant that moves the parcels.

Context uses conservative finite volumes with centered face states, centered diffusion and face-averaged normal velocities derived from the divergence-free Fourier velocity. Their discrete divergence is zero. This keeps the compactly gated pair source exact at lower grid locations and preserves ∫C without pretending a Fourier truncation preserves pointwise support. The context gradient in b_C uses centered differences, making its finite-grid approximation explicit.
8. Chronological reconstruction of encoded increments and a same-total/different-timing response comparison.

`check_coupled_analytic.py` additionally evolves an independent exact-solution control through the same full solver: a decaying transverse shear, a passive context mode, its viscous heating and thermal diffusion, and the corresponding smoothed material trajectory and deformation gradient. Three time steps are compared to analytic formulas. Elastic feedback, history writing and pairing are set to zero for this analytic control; they remain active in the main experiment. Rigid-rotation tests independently check the material energy, stress, conductivity and recording drivers.

`check_coupled_transfer_budget.py` repeats the main trajectory with extra diagnostic counters only. It integrates net advective/conductive heat transport into the fixed region |x| > 0.32 separately from heat generated there by viscosity and expression release. That region is an observation control volume, not an asserted sharp material boundary. The final grid is compared with the uninstrumented main run; a locally generated temperature increase is not counted as transported heat.

[Chen and Peskin's Fourier spectral immersed-boundary method](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.08694) motivates divergence-free interpolation and adjoint interaction work. This implementation uses direct tensor-product interpolation matrices, not their NUFFT implementation or their validated solver. Their convergence results are not imported as evidence for this code.

[Peskin's immersed-boundary formulation](https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/95ECDAC5D1824285563270D6DD70DA9A/S0962492902000077a.pdf/div-class-title-the-immersed-boundary-method-div.pdf), [Bower's constitutive requirements](https://solidmechanics.org/Text/Chapter3_1/Chapter3_1.php) and [Berezovski on internal variables](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10217598/) provide general numerical and thermodynamic context. The specific Hug memory, thermal allocation and upper-half laws remain the additions declared here.

The runnable source is `coupled_hug.py`; the case matrix and batch runner are `run_coupled_suite.py`; the independent checks are `check_coupled_hug.py`. The report must be built from saved outputs and their source hashes. The visualizations show solved material parcels and field slices; no drawing map enforces closure or supplies an uncomputed trajectory.
